package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 HF 5 and others released between March and June 2020
package_info.why_malicious: The Orion software update was compromised by attackers who inserted malicious code (known as Sunburst) into the update package. This code enabled remote access to customer environments, exfiltration of sensitive data, and lateral movement, affecting thousands of organizations including government agencies. The malicious code was not part of the legitimate Orion product and was designed to evade detection and enable espionage.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time and periodically at runtime, the code collects environment information, encodes it, and sends it to a hardcoded command-and-control domain (avsvmcloud.com) via HTTP, then awaits further instructions for remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates unsolicited outbound network connections to an external domain, exfiltrates environment data, and implements a remote command execution backdoor.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion updates should not contain code that beacons to external domains or enables remote command execution by unauthorized parties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or update-checking code may contact vendor servers, but should not exfiltrate environment details or accept arbitrary commands.
key_indicators: Stealthy, delayed beaconing to evade detection

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the Orion update package and distributed to customers via the normal update mechanism.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code on customer systems

attack_chain.action: Upon installation or service startup, the malicious DLL loads and begins beaconing to the attacker's command-and-control server, sending encoded environment information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of C2 channel and victim profiling

attack_chain.action: The attacker issues commands via the C2 channel, enabling remote code execution, lateral movement, and data exfiltration within victim environments.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound HTTP/S requests to avsvmcloud.com or similar C2 domains from Orion processes
Encoded or encrypted environment/system data in network traffic
Orion process spawning unexpected child processes or executing arbitrary commands
file_indicators: Presence of DLLs with unexpected digital signatures or hash mismatches in Orion installation directories
network_indicators: Connections to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure
Unusual HTTP/S traffic patterns from Orion servers to external IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion server processes for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to known C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com). Inspect Orion DLLs for unauthorized code changes or hash mismatches. Analyze network traffic for encoded or suspicious payloads originating from Orion services. Alert on Orion processes executing commands or spawning child processes not typical for normal operation.
